titleStmt.title: Yugoslav Proposal for Article 16 of the Peace Treaty With Italy Submitted to the Council of Foreign Ministers on November 6, 1946

div.head: Yugoslav Proposal for Article 16 of the Peace Treaty With Italy Submitted to the Council of Foreign Ministers on November 6, 1946
div.p: article 16

1. There is hereby constituted the Free City of Trieste, which is recognized by Allied and Associated Powers and by Italy. They agree that the integrity and independence of the Free City of Trieste shall be guaranteed by the Security Council of the United Nations.
2. The frontiers of the Free City of Trieste shall be drawn as follows: (Description of the frontiers)
3. Italian sovereignty over the territory lying within the frontiers described in Paragraph 2 of this Article shall be terminated upon the coming into force of the Treaty.

4. The territory of the Free City shall be neutral and demilitarized. No military forces or para-military formations shall exist, be stationed in, or pass through the Free City, or its territorial waters, or fly over its territory. Peace and order within the territory shall be ensured by the police forces of the Free City itself, which will be recruited solely from among the local population.

5. The Permanent Statute is an integral part of the present Treaty. It shall be submitted to the approval of the Security Council which will report to the General Assembly of the United Nations in accordance with Article 15 of the United Nations Charter.
6. The Permanent Statute shall preserve the following general principles:
a. The governmental structure of the Free City shall be determined by the Constitution enacted by the National Assembly of the Free City. The Constitution shall be in conformity with the Statute.

b. The legislative and executive authority shall be established on democratic lines. The legislative authority shall be exercised by a
National Assembly, elected on the basis of proportional representation by means of a universal, direct, equal and secret suffrage.

The executive authority shall be exercised by the Council of Government, formed by the National Assembly which may also divest it of office. The Council is responsible to the Assembly. All the administrative authorities, including the police and the frontier and coast guards, shall be placed under the Council.
The organization of the judicial authority shall be provided for in the Constitution.

c. The Constitution shall secure to all persons without distinction as to race, sex, national sentiment, language or religion, equal enjoyment of human rights and of the fundamental freedoms, particularly including freedom of expression, of public meeting, of press and publication, of expressing political convictions, of conscience and religious worship, of the use of their own tongue in public and private intercourse, of education and cultural development in their own tongue, and of access to public functions.

d. The Governor shall be appointed by the Security Council after consultation with Yugoslavia and Italy. He shall be responsible to the Security Council as regards the observance of the Statute. For this purpose he is empowered to withhold the promulgation of laws which are contrary to the Statute; the modalities under which these powers will be exercised shall be provided for in the Statute.
The Governor shall submit regular annual reports on his work and on conditions in the territory of the Free City to the Security Council.

e. Domicile in the Free City of Trieste on June 10, 1940, as provided in Article 13 of the Peace Treaty with Italy, shall be qualification for original citizenship of the Free City, provided there has not been option for Italian nationality under this Article.—Those persons who were domiciled in Trieste on October 20, 1918, and subsequently emigrated to Yugoslavia, shall have the right to re-integration into the original citizenship of the Free City.—Those persons who came to this territory from Italy after 1922, and who were militants of the fascist regime or party, war criminals, or were in the service of the Italian police or were civil servants in this territory, shall not be eligible for original citizenship of the Free City.
The conditions for the acquisition of citizenship by persons not qualifying for original citizenship shall be determined by the Assembly of the Free City and embodied in the Constitution.

f. The international regime of the Free Port of Trieste shall ensure the use of the port and of the transit facilities to all goods under equal conditions and irrespective of flag and nationality; Yugoslavia shall, on the other hand, be granted a special free zone in the port. The Free Port shall be outside the customs area of the Free City.

Goods and transport shall be ensured freedom of transit between the port and all the countries served by the port, without any discrimination and without the imposition of any form of customs or fiscal dues for the benefit of the states through whose territory the transit traffic is carried on.

g. In order to secure favorable conditions for the economic development of the Free City of Trieste, cooperation between the Free City and Yugoslavia shall be assured. This cooperation will take the form
of a customs union, of a monetary agreement, of a joint railway administration, of freedom of employment and of settlement for their citizens on a mutual basis, of a joint organization, of the postal, telegraphic and telephone services.

h. For the purpose of ensuring economic cooperation, Yugoslavia shall assume the obligation of representing the Free City and its citizens in relation to foreign countries. Modalities will be provided for under the Statute. Conventions, concluded by Yugoslavia on behalf of the Free City, shall come into force upon ratification by the National Assembly of the Free City.—For the purpose of ensuring this cooperation and of protecting her interests in the Free City, Yugoslavia shall have a political representative in Trieste. He shall be empowered to call the Governor’s attention to any infraction of the Statute and to any encroachment upon the internationally recognized interests of Yugoslavia. In case of dispute, the question shall ex officio be brought before the Security Council.

7. An International Commission for Trieste, consisting of representatives of the United Kingdom, of the USA, of the USSR and of France, shall be formed within a period of one month from the coming into force of the present Treaty. This Commission shall, after consultation with the local political parties and organizations of a democratic character, form the Provisional Government of the Free City, which shall be composed of citizens of Trieste.

The Provisional Government shall, within a period of three months from the date of its formation, carry out elections for the National Assembly which shall form the permanent government and enact the Constitution.
All foreign troops stationed in the Free City shall be withdrawn from the territory within a period of one month from the coming into force of the present Treaty.
8. No changes shall be effected in the Statute without the approval of the Security Council and of Yugoslavia.
